title: Filtering engine v1: allowlist/denylist by category/action/resource
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Beta: adds exporter-side audit event filtering (allow/deny rules) with strict config validation and unit test coverage for edge cases.
description: Implements filtering engine v1 for SIEM-ready audit export (ENG-5160). This adds a small, explicit rule model (allowlist/denylist) that can be evaluated per-event in the exporter with deterministic semantics and safe defaults. Scope in this PR: (1) filter model + evaluation logic (categories/actions/resource predicates), (2) strict config validation + normalization (including “deny wins” and invalid rule rejection), and (3) comprehensive unit tests for tricky cases (empty filters, conflicting allow/deny, unknown categories, wildcard handling, resource/action normalization, timestamp boundary behavior). Motivation: we need customer-configurable filtering that is auditable, easy to reason about during incident response, and stable enough to map to UI + control-plane API without frequent behavior changes. Semantics (as implemented): The effective policy is evaluated in this order: validate -> normalize -> evaluate per event. If filters are absent/null, exporter passes all events (current beta default). If allowlist rules exist, an event must match at least one allow rule to be included. Deny rules always override allow rules (i.e., if an event matches any deny rule, it is excluded even if it also matches allow). Matching: category/action are exact match against canonical strings; resource matching supports resource.type exact match, and resource.id supports either exact match or a simple prefix pattern of the form "prefix:*" (to support common shapes like "workspace:*" without introducing a full glob/regex surface). If a rule specifies multiple fields, the rule matches only if all specified fields match (AND). If a filter list contains unknown categories/actions (not in the exporter’s current taxonomy allowlist), config is rejected and exporter will not start that tenant’s pipeline (surfaced as config error + status). This is intentional for beta to avoid silently dropping/including unexpected events; we can revisit “unknown = no match” for GA if we need forward-compat behavior. Notes: This PR is aligned with ADR-audit-export-filtering-model (allow/deny + deterministic evaluation) and keeps the API surface minimal. The control plane is expected to perform the same validation; exporter validation is defense-in-depth in case of stale/buggy configs. Follow-ups: (a) wire up exporter status endpoint to include “filter_validation_error” details (truncated/safe) for Console, (b) add microbench for high-volume match evaluation, (c) consider forward-compat for new categories (feature-flagged behavior) once schema v2 taxonomy is stable. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for matching + precedence - [x] Validation errors are structured and redact sensitive fields - [x] Metrics: counter for filtered_out_total by tenant + category (bounded cardinality) - [x] Docs snippet added to internal README for config examples - [ ] E2E coverage will land in ENG-5195 (separate PR)
commits: filter: implement matcher for category/action/resource predicates
validation: reject unknown categories/actions; enforce max rule counts
tests: add table-driven tests for precedence + wildcard prefix
docs: add config examples + semantics notes
code_snippets: Pseudo-config example used in tests: allow: [{category: "auth", action: "token.create"}, {category: "admin", resource_type: "audit_export"}] deny: [{category: "admin", action: "rbac.policy.update"}, {resource_type: "workspace", resource_id: "workspace:prod-*"}] // deny wins; allow required if allowlist non-empty
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): Can we confirm deny > allow is explicit and tested? Also, please ensure validation errors don’t echo full resource IDs (could be sensitive).

Jordan Lee (Author): Yes—added table-driven tests for overlap and a unit test asserting deny wins. Validation errors now include only rule index + field name + reason; resource_id values are not printed (only length + whether prefix-pattern was used).
Ethan Park (Platform): How strict should we be about unknown categories/actions? If schema adds a new category, we might block exports until the exporter is updated.

Jordan Lee (Author): Agreed risk. For beta I leaned strict to avoid “silent wrong” behavior. I added a TODO + comment in validation.go to revisit and potentially feature-flag forward-compat (unknown => no match) once taxonomy stabilizes. This also matches what Console will display (explicit config error).
Benji Okafor (Control Plane): Please document max rule counts and the prefix pattern format. UI needs to mirror this. Also confirm matcher is allocation-free in the hot path.

Jordan Lee (Author): Updated README with max rules (allow<=50, deny<=50 per config, total<=100) and prefix pattern is "<prefix>*" with a required trailing "*". Matcher uses pre-normalized structs + string comparisons; no regex and no per-event allocations in the core match loop (verified with go test -run TestMatcher_NoAllocs).
Kevin Osei (Security/Compliance): One more ask: include metric for filtered events, but keep labels bounded. Don’t label on action/resource_id.
Jordan Lee (Author): Done—metric is filtered_out_total labeled by tenant_id (internal), destination_id (small bounded set per tenant), and category only. No action/resource labels.
Marcus Lin (Security): Approved once the error messages are confirmed redacted.
Jordan Lee (Author): Pushed follow-up commit; errors now use "rule[3].resource_id: invalid prefix pattern" without values. Added tests that assert error string does not contain provided resource IDs.
post_merge_notes: Reminder: keep exporter + control-plane validation in sync. If taxonomy changes (schema v2), update exporter’s known category/action list and consider feature-flagging forward-compat behavior before widening beta cohort.
